pass_type: FREEZE ADDENDUM 4 directed position-in-container Track-B pass

criteria.name: Header pointing readers to the author's own earlier post
criteria.instruction: Read the first three and last three lines for an explicit external dependency: a link or note saying this is a prologue, a part one, a continuation, or that another piece should be read first. Record 0 (self-contained), 1 (the story silently assumes prior events, introducing a world or cast as already known to the reader), or 2 (an explicit continuation header or link). Separately record whether the piece parses for a reader who has not seen the other piece.
criteria.upstream_parent: Whether this entry is a fresh top-level reply or a continuation of the author's own earlier reply or post.
criteria.rationale: R04 opens with a bare link, 'Prologue from here: http://...', before any prose. R34 opens 'This is a continuation of [another story] ... This will make more sense if you read part 1 first'. Both fingerprint a second entry in an author's own chain, which sits differently in the reply order than a cold top-level post. Mixed because a continuation is written on top of a world and cast already built, which can genuinely deepen the prose.

criteria.name: Revision-trail disclosure
criteria.instruction: Score visible edit notes, addenda, revision counters, postscript explanations, or author comments indicating changes after the initial submission.
criteria.upstream_parent: How long after the prompt appeared the story was written
criteria.rationale: R12 describes revising the opening, updating a revision counter, and adding an addendum; R35 uses a post-divider author note to reassess the finished story. Later editing can change both reception and actual finish quality.

criteria.name: Prior-thread reaction
criteria.instruction: Score explicit language or conspicuous framing that presents the story as an alternative to an obvious, expected, or already-used response.
criteria.upstream_parent: Whether other replies already existed that this one reacts to or differentiates itself from
criteria.rationale: R02 rejects the expected empty meta treatment of the prompt and chooses a counter-angle; R08 makes a conspicuous crossover choice around a recognizable opening line. Differentiation can itself produce genuinely more original writing.

criteria.name: Audience-facing aftercare
criteria.instruction: Score authorial notes, word counts, feedback requests, self-assessments, or archive links appended after the story as evidence of submission-stage behavior.
criteria.upstream_parent: Whether the item was posted as a standalone thread reply for an established reply audience
criteria.rationale: R06 appends a word count, subreddit reference, and closing comment; R35 adds a promotional subreddit note and post-publication reflection. This reveals posting context, not intrinsic story quality.

criteria.name: Thread-context references
criteria.instruction: Score explicit references to the prompt board, prompt stream, other submissions, or the act of replying, apart from the fictional narrative.
criteria.upstream_parent: Whether other replies already existed that this one was reacting to
criteria.rationale: R12 discusses encountering another meta prompt and deciding to write in response; R38 describes writing in response to one of these posts and requests community criticism. Such context can shape deliberate positioning as well as reception.

criteria.name: Prefatory note or restated tag before the narrative begins
criteria.instruction: Check whether the text opens with a short framing line before the story proper starts -- an off-topic aside about the prompt or its accompanying image, or a title line restating the prompt's tag -- rather than beginning directly in-scene. Note presence/absence only.
criteria.upstream_parent: how long after the prompt appeared the story was written (and therefore how much time the writer had)
criteria.rationale: R08 opens with 'Off-topic writer's note: Goddamn, that's a cool picture' and R07 opens with a title line '(WP) Party of Five' before the scene starts -- both read as a same-sitting reaction captured on the page, plausibly indicating the piece was drafted immediately after seeing the prompt rather than after a delay.

criteria.name: No read-through pass: inconsistencies a reread would catch
criteria.instruction: Count inconsistencies that only a second reading of the writer's own text would catch: a name spelled two ways within the same piece, a tense that flips mid-paragraph, a dropped or doubled word inside a sentence, a character called by the wrong name. Report the count and whether any fall in the first 200 words. Do not score vocabulary, formatting, punctuation style, or dialect spelling.
criteria.upstream_parent: Length of the composition window between the prompt appearing and the reply being posted, and whether there was time for a reread before submitting.
criteria.rationale: R12 alternates 'Gray' and 'Grey' for the same dragon inside one page and writes 'when them toss me out' and 'Fist Aid Kit'. R03 flips present to past inside its own opening ('Pressing my hand... it was quite a sight to see') and carries 'I pictures the strange red fire' and 'I'm shock'. R05 carries 'alieans', 'exestential' and 'plen ty'. These are reread failures rather than typography or house style, and they are honestly mixed: a longer window really does buy cleaner prose as well as an earlier slot forgone.

criteria.name: Retrofitted-work markers
criteria.instruction: Score explicit prologue, excerpt, prior-draft, or external-story framing suggesting the text existed before this prompt.
criteria.upstream_parent: Whether the story was retrofitted from material the author already had
criteria.rationale: R13 identifies an earlier linked story in the same fictional sequence; R26 presents its text as a prologue from another linked work. Reusing prior material can also produce more polished writing.

criteria.name: Story ends without narrative resolution (cliffhanger/mid-arc cutoff)
criteria.instruction: Check whether the piece ends before its central conflict or question is resolved -- e.g. trailing off on an open threat, an undecided action, or a scene-break mark with no follow-through -- versus reaching a clear resolution or beat. Note presence/absence only.
criteria.upstream_parent: how long after the prompt appeared the story was written (and therefore how much time the writer had)
criteria.rationale: R07 ends on the antagonist's open threat ('What will you do now, Cap?') followed only by a scene-break mark, and R24 ends mid-standoff on 'Maybe' with the confrontation unresolved -- both stop short of a resolved ending, a pattern consistent with running out of composition time before posting.

criteria.name: Compressed submission form
criteria.instruction: Score unusually compressed, fragmentary, or submission-like formatting when it appears to reflect a narrow composition or posting window.
criteria.upstream_parent: How long after the prompt appeared the story was written
criteria.rationale: R19 is a very short poem with a minimal completion marker, while R21 consists only of an automated tagging response rather than a developed story. Time pressure can produce this form, although compression may also be intentional craft.
